title: Reply to @theatreislife  #greenscreen #everybodystalkinaboutjamie @ja...
transcript: yes it was *that* good. listen: I love this show I love the stage version I love the scrappiness of its storytelling I love the source material it's based on I think the message it conveys is relevant and heartfelt and just full of love and joy and the movie version which is so hard to do in a film adaptation of a stage musical elevates everything I loved about the stage version and any changes they made I thought were really smart to serve the storytelling especially for a movie adaptation for example “The legend of Loco Channelle” — I think is the name of the song it was a throwaway number didn't really add much to the plot it was kind of a road bump for me in the show. so the song they replaced it with is a flashback sequence hugo, in his mentorship role to jamie, can talk about what it really meant to be a drag queen in the eighties during the height of the AIDS epidemic and the person who plays the young Loco Chanelle in a flashback sequence is a brilliant stroke of genius in terms of cameo casting also check out the documentary “jamie: drag queen at 16” it's on amazon prime you can rent it for $2
